name: Four Card Poker
description: Four Card Poker is a popular casino table game that pits the player against the house. Similar to Three Card Poker, it is a game of decision-making and hand valuation, but with a unique twist: the dealer receives a significant card advantage (six cards to the player's five) to offset the fact that the dealer does not need to 'qualify' to play. Despite the name, players and the dealer use their best four-card hand from their respective totals, leading to a unique ranking system where Three-of-a-Kind actually beats a Flush.

history.origins: Designed by Roger Snow and owned by Shuffle Master (now part of Light & Wonder), Four Card Poker was released as a follow-up to the massive success of Three Card Poker. It was engineered to provide more aggressive betting options (up to 3x Ante) while maintaining a low entry barrier for casual gamblers.
timeline: Early 2000s: Introduced to Las Vegas casinos.
2005-2010: Becomes a standard fixture in casino pits nationwide.
Present: One of the 'Big Three' specialty poker games alongside Three Card Poker and Ultimate Texas Hold'em.
history.cultural: Known for the 'Aces Up' side bet, which allows players to win big payouts regardless of whether they beat the dealer.
history.evolution: The game's hand rankings were mathematically tuned to account for the four-card format, specifically making Three-of-a-Kind rare enough to outrank both Straights and Flushes.

setup.players: Typically 1 to 6 players seated at a specialized casino table.
setup.deck: One standard 52-card deck, usually shuffled by a machine after every hand.
setup.dealing: The Player receives 5 cards. The Dealer receives 6 cards (one of which is turned face up).

rules.objective: Form a better four-card poker hand than the dealer.
rules.gameplay:
1. Players place an Ante bet.
2. Cards are dealt. Players examine their 5-card hand and choose the best 4-card combination.
3. Making a Choice: Players must either FOLD (losing the Ante) or make a PLAY bet.
4. Play Bet: Unlike other games, you can bet 1x, 2x, or 3x your Ante.
5. The Showdown: The Dealer reveals their 6 cards and makes their best 4-card hand. There is no 'dealer qualify' rule.
keyRules: Automatic Bonus: If the player has a Three-of-a-Kind or better, they win a bonus on the Ante bet, regardless of the dealer's hand.
Aces Up: This side bet pays if the player has at least a Pair of Aces in their best four-card hand.

strategy.basic: Strategy is simpler than it looks. You should play (bet 1x) if you have any pair of 10s or better. If you have less than 10s, you should fold.
strategy.intermediate: The 3x Bet: Whenever you have a Pair of Aces or better (including any Three-of-a-Kind), you should always bet the maximum (3x). The statistical advantage on these hands is too large to ignore.
strategy.advanced: Dealer Upcard Analysis: If the dealer's visible face-up card is higher than your best card, and you only have a low pair (e.g. 2s or 3s), consider folding even if you 'should' play by the 10s rule, as the dealer has 5 other chances to beat you.
tips: Never bet 2x. Statistically, you should either bet 1x (to see the hand) or 3x (on a winner). The middle ground is mathematically inferior.
Don't chase the Aces Up bet unless you are prepared for high volatility; the house edge is significantly higher than the standard game.
